newsitem.title: UK: BA again postpones UK-Israel cargo date.
newsitem.headline: BA again postpones UK-Israel cargo date.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo said it has postponed planned UK-Israel cargo flights for the third time this year and is now looking at mid-June, end-September or even late-1997 as the start-up date.

Outsourcing manager of BA Cargo Graham Bunsell told Reuters the reason for the delays was that the aircraft BA planned to use -- Channel Express's first Airbus A300B4 freighter -- had not received U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) operating authorisation.
The former passenger A300B4 has undergone conversion into full-freighter configuration by British Aerospace Aviation Services at BAe's Filton plant, near Bristol.

"It may seem strange that FAA approval (of the conversion) is needed but that would mean the aircraft had achieved a worldwide, acceptable standard," Bunsell said in a telephone interview. "Local authorisation, for instance in this case by the UK CAA (Civil Aviation Authority) might inhibit us in using the aircraft on some routes around the world, including to and from Israel," he added.

Bunsell said that BA had first planned to start once-weekly London Gatwick-Tel Aviv services with the A300B4 freighter on wet-lease from Channel Express -- involving the hire of both aircraft and crew -- from January 23.

"Because of the FAA problems, the launch was put back to February 20 and then May 1. Now we are looking at the end of June or if that doesn't work, the end of September. Otherwise it might be later in the year," he said.
He added that Pisa, Italy, would "almost certainly" be included as a stopover on the Tel Aviv-London leg of the proposed new service.
The plan is now to operate twice-weekly frequencies on the route from Stansted instead of Gatwick, where BA is coming under landing and take-off slot pressure, said BA sources.
No spokesman at Channel Express, a member of the Dart Group of Companies, was available for comment on the FAA's delay in approving the conversion of its 40-tonne capacity A300 freighter.
BA World Cargo has been tring to win agreement to operate cargo charters to and from Israel for at least two-and-a-half years but has been thwarted on each occasion.

Objections made by Israel since 1994 have covered BA's proposals to use either ageing aircraft which do not meet modern "Chapter 2" noise levels and suggesting planes for use on the route that are not registered by the UK CAA, the BA sources noted.
